words.sense: Grant the right to vote or participate fully in civic political life
misconceptions: Treating freedom from control as the same as voting rights.
Assuming the right to vote eliminates all other restrictions.

words.sense: Release someone from legal, social, or political subjection
misconceptions: Treating freedom from control as the same as voting rights.
Using liberation language for a change only to the electoral roll.

semantic_axes.description: Enfranchise grants voting or civic political rights; emancipate releases a person from imposed legal or social control.

edges.boundary_rule: Enfranchise grants voting or civic political rights; emancipate releases a person from imposed legal or social control.

misconceptions.M1: Treating freedom from control as the same as voting rights.
misconceptions.M2: Assuming the right to vote eliminates all other restrictions.
misconceptions.M3: Using liberation language for a change only to the electoral roll.

chains.frame: Which word best describes what the council decision does for Dina?

beats.text: Dina has lived in the town for years but could not vote; a new rule now permits her to cast a ballot.
beats.decisive_clue: new eligibility to vote in local government
beats.reason: The initial evidence is new eligibility to vote in local government; it best supports enfranchise.

beats.text: Her name is added to the official voter register before the next election.
beats.decisive_clue: formal inclusion on the voting roll
beats.reason: Registration confirms the new electoral right, not release from personal control.

chains.feedback_short: Registration confirms the new electoral right, not release from personal control.
chains.feedback_deep: Enfranchise means give formal political voting rights; emancipate means set free from binding authority or control. Registration confirms the new electoral right, not release from personal control.
chains.contrast_rule: Enfranchise gives a political voice; emancipate removes a controlling bond.

beats.text: After years under a legal guardian's control, Asha is declared independent and can make her own contracts.
beats.reason: The initial evidence is release from legal guardianship; it best supports emancipate.

beats.text: She can now sign her own rental agreement without requesting anyone's permission.
beats.decisive_clue: legal independence from another person's control
beats.reason: Signing alone is evidence of independence rather than a new voting right.

beats.text: A binding agreement once barred Bilal from leaving his employer; the court voids it and he can resign freely.
beats.reason: The initial evidence is release from a coercive contract; it best supports emancipate.

beats.text: He celebrates with a meal at his favourite cafe.
beats.reason: The celebration does not change the fact that a controlling obligation was lifted.
